applicant_utility.summary: A CERN research fellowship is a paid employment contract, not a studentship: the CHF 7,004-7,425 net monthly stipend is the salary you live on, with health insurance and pension contributions attached. Recruitment runs vacancy by vacancy, so you apply to one specific advertised post (currently Research Fellowship: Theoretical Physics, closing 2 November 2026) and each field of work runs its own separate competition. Before investing effort, check the nationality rule on the programme page: nationals of six Member and Associate Member States are currently excluded while the Article II.5 ceiling is reached.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent PhDs in theoretical or experimental physics, or in applied sciences and engineering, from eligible CERN Member or Associate Member States, within the research-experience cap and with no prior CERN fellow or graduate contract.
application_readiness_checklist: Line up three referees before you submit: the confidential submission link reaches them only after your application is filed, and letters must be under one year old at the deadline
Draft the statement of research interests in advance, since the advertised Theoretical Physics vacancy requires it explicitly
Re-check the nationality exclusion list on the programme page immediately before applying
Prepare a CV in English or French and block out about 15 minutes for the online form
If your paper PhD diploma is not yet issued, request a certificate of achievement from your university now
common_rejection_risks: Missing the per-vacancy deadline, or assuming an application in one field carries over to Experimental Physics, Applied Science and Engineering or Theoretical Physics, which are separate competitions
Having previously held any CERN fellow or graduate contract, or being a current CERN Staff member, both of which are disqualifying
Exceeding the research-experience cap as measured at the application deadline (6 years for physics, 3 years for engineering, exceptionally 6)
Recommendation letters that are older than one year at the deadline
Holding an excluded nationality while the Article II.5 ceiling is reached
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything beyond the conditional installation grant and travel to Geneva: CERN states it offers no direct relocation assistance, so housing deposits, removals and initial living costs in the Geneva area before the first salary fall on the fellow, as do family costs not met by the child and infant allowances.
document_audit: The CV must be in English or French
A university certificate of achievement is accepted in place of a diploma that has not yet been issued
Recommendation letters are uploaded by the referees through their own confidential link, not by you
The specific vacancy may add documents beyond the programme-level list, so read the vacancy page, not only the programme overview
The research-experience cap is counted at the application deadline, so document your PhD completion date precisely
alerts: The advertised Theoretical Physics vacancy closes 02/11/2026 at 23:59 Geneva time for an ideal start of 01/10/2027, so plan around Geneva time, not your local zone

applicant_utility.submission_workflow: File one online application on the CERN careers portal against the named vacancy, trigger the referee link, await the hiring-manager interview decision, then accept the offer and move into onboarding.

applicant_utility.summary: IMD scholarships are not standalone applications: you are only in contention once you hold an accepted offer, and the request is made inside the Program section of the MBA application form itself. The award is a deduction against programme cost, taken off the fourth and third installments and never the first two, so you must still fund the CHF 10,000 deposit and CHF 22,500 second instalment yourself, on top of roughly CHF 36,000 of Lausanne living costs. With the final 2027-intake round closing 13 October 2026 and awards allocated only until the pool runs out, applying in an early round is materially safer than waiting.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong GMAT/GRE performers with three to eight years of career progression and international exposure who are not company-sponsored, particularly women applicants and STEM-background candidates for the named awards.
application_readiness_checklist: Sit the GMAT/GRE early: the score must be under five years old, with a test-taker copy uploaded and an official score report ordered for IMD (GMAT code SKR-MM-13, GRE code 8490)
Rebuild your CV on IMD's one-page template; any other format is refused
Brief your recommender early and make sure they submit from a professional email address, ideally two weeks before your chosen round
Order official English or French translations of every diploma and transcript, including the grading scale
Budget the CHF 150 application fee and the CHF 10,000 non-refundable first instalment due two to four weeks after an offer
common_rejection_risks: Being company-sponsored, which rules you out of scholarships entirely
Counting on stacking awards: scholarships are non-cumulative and you will not be selected for more than one
An incomplete file, which gets pushed to the next round and can arrive after the allocation pool is exhausted
A generic MBA5 essay: the 750-word question asks specifically about your contribution to the class and your impact beyond graduation
A weak assessment day, since performance there is an explicit criterion for every named award
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Published living costs average CHF 36,000 for a single person in Lausanne (about CHF 3,000 a month), plus the CHF 32,500 of first and second installments that scholarships cannot touch, the CHF 150 application fee, and Swiss registration and residence taxes that are higher for non-European nationals.
